# @ratmath/logic

> Formal logic for RatMath: propositional and predicate logic, proof checking, model search, modal logic and computability. Part of the RatMath Shelf; numbers come from @ratmath/core (a peer dependency). ESM: `import * as logic from "@ratmath/logic"`.

Built from 0.2.0, commit 2753c30 plus uncommitted changes. `file:line` is relative to the package root (also node_modules/@ratmath/logic/); on GitHub: https://github.com/ratmath/logic/blob/2753c30/<file>#L<line>. Docs pages are under https://ratmath.com/logic/. Full types: index.d.ts.

Types: `type Kind = "atom" | "top" | "bot" | "not" | "and" | "or" | "imp" | "iff" | "xor"`; `type Style = "unicode" | "ascii" | "words" | "tex"`; `type FormulaLike = Formula | string`; `type FormulaList = readonly FormulaLike[] | string | Formula`; `type Valuation = Record<string, boolean | 0 | 1> | Map<string, boolean | 0 | 1>`; `type Model = Record<string, boolean>`; `type ClauseLike = string | readonly string[]`; `type Citation = number | [number, number]`; `type FOKind = "pred" | "eq" | "top" | "bot" | "not" | "and" | "or" | "imp" | "iff" | "xor" | "all" | "ex"`; `type FOFormulaLike = FOFormula | string`; `type FOFormulaList = readonly FOFormulaLike[] | string | FOFormula`; `type Element = string | number`; `type GateKind = "and" | "or" | "xor" | "nand" | "nor" | "xnor" | "not" | "buf"`; `type CategoricalForm = "A" | "E" | "I" | "O"`; `type ModalSystem = "K" | "D" | "T" | "B" | "S4" | "S5"`; `type AutomatonLike = Automaton | AutomatonSpec`

## Docs

- https://ratmath.com/logic/llms-full.txt: every page below as Markdown, each with a runnable example
- Pages: index (Overview), reference (Reference), explore (Explore), formulas (Formulas), truth-tables (Truth tables), normal-forms (Normal forms), satisfiability (Satisfiability and validity), simplification (Simplification), natural-deduction (Natural deduction), sequents (Sequent calculus), truth-trees (Truth trees), resolution (Resolution), proof-search (Proof search and hints), predicate-logic (Predicate logic), models (Finite models), first-order-proofs (First-order proofs and trees), circuits (Circuits and Karnaugh maps), syllogisms (Syllogisms), modal-logic (Modal logic), automata (Automata and regular expressions), machines (Grammars and machines)

## Example

```js
import { entails, proveSequent, tableauProof, prove } from "@ratmath/logic";
// Is this argument valid? Ask four ways, and look at the evidence each gives.
const premises = "p -> q, q -> r";
const conclusion = "p -> r";

console.log("by the solver:  ", entails(premises, conclusion).status);
console.log("by a truth tree:", tableauProof(premises, conclusion).status);
console.log("by sequents:    ", proveSequent(premises + " |- " + conclusion).status);
const found = prove(premises, conclusion);
console.log("by natural deduction:\n" + found.proof);

// Change the conclusion to "r -> p" and every method returns the same countermodel instead.
entails(premises, "r -> p").countermodel
```
